overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by improperly discussing a personnel matter in executive session and by failing to notify candidates before the executive session. Violations found intentional; referred to hearing with a recommended $2,000 fine and minutes release orders.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed matters in its August 31 executive session that were not appropriate for executive session.
allegations.key_passage: By discussing this personnel matter behind closed doors, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board convened executive session under Purpose 1 to discuss job candidates' background checks without giving the candidates written notice 48 hours in advance.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Board's failure to notify the candidates of the executive session clearly violated the Open Meeting Law's requirements for convening in executive session under Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Whether the Board may withhold the August 31 executive session minutes concerning the discussion of candidates' release forms and background checks.
allegations.key_passage: The Board may not redact or withhold that portion of the minutes in any way.

remedy: Civil penalty of $2,000 total ($1,000 per intentional violation), recommended after referral to a hearing under 940 CMR 29.07(3).
Release the August 31 executive session minutes concerning the release-form discussion to the public, unredacted.
Provide the three candidates who were the subjects of the executive session with an unredacted version of the minutes concerning themselves within thirty days of receipt of the determination.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to release to the public the executive session minutes concerning this discussion.
